title: Security & Compliance Review: Cross-Border Guardrails for Riverbend Health
summary: High-level compliance review for Riverbend Health focused on ensuring EU/US data residency controls, KMS key boundary requirements, and sub-processor commitments. Agreement to validate network and flow diagrams, run a short proof-of-traffic test, and provide SOC2/ISO artifacts + subprocessor roster. Action items assigned for DPA/KMS follow-up and SSO integration checklist.
action_items: Priya Kapoor: Provide Riverbend network diagram and list of EU-processing apps (due: 2026-06-25)
Jordan Patel: Share Redwood KMS integration guide and sample policy (due: 2026-06-22)
Marta Silva: Run a 48h pilot config with EU-region pinning and report latency/cost delta (due: 2026-06-30)
Samir Qureshi: Send questions on subprocessor CLA and DPA redlines (due: 2026-06-24)
Ava Martinez: Share SOC2 Type II summary, ISO cert snapshot, and subprocessor list (due: 2026-06-21)
next_steps: Redwood to share docs: SOC2 summary, subprocessor roster, KMS-ops note
Customer to hand over network diagram and target workloads for EU pinning
Schedule pilot start call the week of 2026-06-22
Legal teams to exchange DPA redlines after pilot results
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Marta (Redwood SE), Daniel (Riverbend CISO), Priya (Head Cloud Ops), Samir (Legal), Emily (SRE)
---
[00:00] Ava (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, can you confirm names?
[00:12] Daniel (Riverbend): Daniel here.
[00:15] Priya: Priya, hi.
[00:17] Samir: Samir on legal.
[00:18] Emily: Emily, SRE.
[00:22] Ava: Great. Goal for today is to walk through data residency controls, region pinning, KMS boundary questions and sub-processor commitments. We'll also talk about audit logs and SSO. Jordan will handle some of the technical details.
[00:35] Jordan (Redwood): Hi all, quick note — my screen is up, I put a short architecture slide in the chat, link: https://redwood.ai/docs/region-pinning (please ping if you don't see).
[00:52] Priya: Got it. Our ask up front: Riverbend needs firm guarantees that EU patient data never leaves EU processing nodes and that keys are customer-controlled where required. We also need an inventory of subprocessors and how data flows to them.
[01:10] Ava: Understood. High level — Redwood supports config-level region affinity and can route workloads to EU-only clusters. For KMS we have two models — Redwood-managed KMS with our FR-handles keys, or customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (bring-your-own-key).
[01:30] Daniel: When you say "route to EU clusters" is that soft affinity or hard boundary? We need a contractual guarantee — no cross-border processing for pinned data sets.
[01:44] Jordan: Today the runtime can be pinned by tenant+route. We're able to put your pinned workload on EU-only nodes and avoid cross-region egress. The caveat is third-party subprocessors — some observability vendors might touch telemetry metadata unless we exclude them.
[02:05] Emily: On telemetry — we need to know what logging is emitted to Redwood control plane. Any PII or patient identifiers in logs?
[02:16] Marta (Redwood): Good question. By default we scrub prompt/response payloads from control-plane logs unless you opt-in to advanced logging. We emit trace ids, latency metrics, and anonymized error signatures. I will double-check exact fields — I think we do not store full prompt text by default.
[02:38] Samir: Can you confirm retention windows for those logs and where they are stored geographically?
[02:45] Jordan: Control plane logs are stored in the region of the control plane; for Hosted customers control plane is in US by default. For Private and Dedicated we can run control plane in your VPC in EU. For customers who require EU-residency for logs we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with EU control plane.
[03:05] Priya: So we would need a private control plane in an EU region to ensure everything, including audit logs, remains in EU?
[03:12] Ava: Yes, that's the strongest guarantee. There's also hybrid — you can use Redwood hosted inference nodes in EU and request that audit logs be forwarded to your EU logging account via a controlled sink. But that's more of a configuration and we should capture the exact flow.
[03:30] Daniel: About KMS — we have a policy that patient-sensitive models must use customer-managed keys with no key export. How does Redwood integrate with Cloud KMS or HSM?
[03:43] Jordan: We support Cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault) and we have a conservative integration: the customer keeps key lifecycle and Redwood requests encrypt/decrypt operations through a signed mTLS channel. No key material leaves your KMS. For HSM-backed KMS, we can support external calls but we need a small connector to your VPC.
[04:07] Priya: Is there support for key-scoping by region? e.g., a key that is allowed only for EU nodes?
[04:15] Marta: Yes, you can scope keys by policy and we can map workloads to a key alias that is restricted to EU projects. We'll surface recommended IAM policies in the KMS integration guide.
[04:30] Samir: We need the KMS audit trail as well — every decrypt call logged with requester and timestamp. Does Redwood preserve and surface that?
[04:40] Jordan: We log KMS request IDs and can surface an audit export to your SIEM; if you're using customer-managed KMS then the primary key audit trail lives in your KMS (so you get the canonical record). Redwood will keep a reference-level log with request ID and nonce.
[04:58] Priya: On subprocessors — we've seen many vendors list a long chain. Can you provide a current subprocessor roster and the role they play? Also, do you allow veto or pushback on new subprocessors?
[05:13] Ava: We maintain a live subprocessor list and will share it. Typically for Hosted customers we cannot guarantee veto but we give 30-day notice for material changes. For Enterprise Private deployments, you can negotiate more restrictive CLAs and we can exclude certain subprocessors.
[05:31] Daniel: What about cross-border subprocessors? If a subprocessor is US-based but processes metadata for EU requests, that's a deal breaker for us.
[05:42] Jordan: In practice, we can configure routing to avoid sending payloads to those subprocessors; however telemetry metadata routing depends on your chosen logging path. We'll flag any subprocessor that touches unredacted payloads.
[06:00] Emily: Latency concerns — pinning to EU will add some cost/throughput tradeoffs. Can we see benchmarks of token throughput and 95th percentile lat for EU-only clusters vs default?
[06:12] Marta: Yes, we can run a 48-hour pilot to capture p95 and cost delta — that'll give real-world numbers on your workload. We'll need a sample traffic pattern from you.
[06:25] Priya: We'll provide example workload and SLAs. Also can you support private peering between our VPC and Redwood EU nodes?
[06:34] Jordan: Yes, private peering or VPC VPN is supported for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we can do mutual TLS and IP allow lists but not private peering.
[06:46] Samir: Regarding certifications — we require SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence. Do you have those and are they current?
[06:54] Ava: Yes, Redwood has SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications. I'll share the cover letter and the auditor's summary. Note that the full reports are shared under NDA.
[07:05] Daniel: Good. Also need clarification on encryption in transit and at rest. For at rest, does Redwood encrypt model caches on GPU with customer keys?
[07:16] Jordan: Model artifact storage can be encrypted with your keys in Dedicated/Private. On GPU, memory is ephemeral; we do NVME cache which is encrypted; again you can provide keys for the storage in Dedicated setups. For hosted where we manage keys, we encrypt at rest with provider keys and apply disk-level encryption.
[07:40] Emily: If an attacker got access to a node, how quickly can you purge a tenant's KV cache?
[07:47] Marta: We support immediate cache invalidation per-tenant via an API and can audit purge operations in the control plane logs. We'll share the API call in the follow-up.
[08:00] Priya: What about data subject requests — e.g., right to be forgotten — is there a standard workflow?
[08:07] Ava: We support deletion APIs and region-scoped deletions; however, please note that model weights and knowledge baked into a model are not reversible in general. We recommend minimizing persistent storage of raw PII and using ephemeral in-memory processing or redaction before send. We'll work with you on retention windows and deletion semantics.
[08:28] Daniel: Okay. Let's dig into a slightly hairy corner: control plane metadata — do you replicate metadata to US services for observability?
[08:38] Jordan: For Hosted, yes some control-plane telemetry may route through our centralized services in the US. For EU-only requirement, Private or Dedicated with EU control plane is required. We can also set up log forwarding to your EU logging with no retention in the US.
[08:56] Samir: You mentioned notices for subprocessors — what's the timeframe and process for objecting?
[09:02] Ava: We send a 30-day notice for material subprocessors and provide a simple opt-out for Enterprise customers during contract negotiation. Post-signing we'd have to negotiate exclusion clauses.
[09:13] Priya: On SSO — we use SAML with SCIM for user provisioning. How does Redwood integrate for RBAC and audit of API tokens?
[09:22] Jordan: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. For RBAC you can map groups to roles and we log token issuance. Tokens can be rotated automatically and we provide token audit exports.
[09:36] Emily: Do API tokens ever travel to US-based services?
[09:40] Marta: Token issuance metadata may go through our issuer endpoint; for EU control plane, issuance occurs in-region.
[09:48] Daniel: A follow-up on legal — what's in the DPA re: cross-border processing and subprocessor liability?
[09:54] Ava: The DPA includes standard SCCs (or equivalent) and enumerates subprocessors; liability is negotiated at enterprise. Samir, we'll set a time for legal teams to exchange specific redlines.
[10:06] Samir: We'll want a dedicated clause preventing onward transfer of unredacted patient data outside EU without consent.
[10:14] Ava: That can be discussed and is typically handled in the DPA + subprocessor addendum.
[10:20] Jordan: One operational note — for the pilot we'll create a pinned route and specific model variant that reduces token caching outside EU. The pilot is the best way to surface unexpected metadata leaks.
[10:33] Priya: Sounds good. We'll provide a traffic sample.
[10:36] Ava: Great. Any other technical concerns?
[10:39] Emily: What about backups and snapshots — do you have backups that might be stored outside the region?
[10:45] Jordan: We snapshot model artifacts and config; for Dedicated we can keep snapshots in your project bucket. For hosted, snapshots may be in provider-controlled buckets; we can configure retention and region for Enterprise.
[11:02] Daniel: Can you clarify what 'scrubbing' means in practice? Is it regex-based or ML-based PII detection?
[11:10] Marta: We use a combination: simple regex-based masking for common patterns plus optional ML PII detectors you can enable. We'll document default scrubbing rules.
[11:26] Priya: We want to run an ingress filter on our side as well — double filter.
[11:30] Ava: Good practice.\n[12:00] Jordan: I'm going to show a short sequence diagram — small chance of mislabel on my screen share — but it shows client -> Redwood EU node -> KMS in EU via customer-managed key, and audit events forwarded to customer SIEM.
[12:22] Daniel: Looks good, though I see a US control plane arrow in the diagram — can that be removed in EU-only config?
[12:31] Jordan: Yes, if you go Private/Dedicated with EU control plane the arrow disappears; for Hosted you'd have some minimal control-plane interaction in US unless we spin up EU control plane for you.
[12:46] Priya: Estimated timeline — how fast can we get EU Dedicated cluster provisioned for pilot?
[12:52] Marta: For Dedicated it's usually 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and legal onboarding. For Private VPC it can be 4-8 weeks. A hosted EU pin with config changes can be tried in 3-5 days as a light pilot.
[13:08] Emily: Cost delta for Dedicated vs hosted pilot?
[13:12] Ava: We'll put numbers in the cost spreadsheet but expect Dedicated to have higher base commit with lower per-token for high throughput; hosted EU pinning will be higher per-token with lower upfront.
[13:27] Samir: Regarding audit logs retention — we have a 7-year requirement for certain access logs. Can Redwood retain logs that long?
[13:36] Jordan: We can support long-tail retention as an add-on for Enterprise. By default retention is 90 days. Long retention requires secure export to your long-term storage or an add-on contract.
[13:50] Priya: What's the mechanism for exporting logs to our SIEM?
[13:55] Marta: We provide a push-based secure connector that ships logs to your S3/GCS/Azure blob or to common SIEM endpoints over TLS with authentication.
[14:05] Daniel: On the topic of cross-border KMS access — if the KMS is in EU but Redwood has worker nodes in US for some reason, would decrypts cross the border?
[14:13] Jordan: If a worker outside EU needs to decrypt with your key, by default yes that would be a cross-border request. That's why we recommend locked EU-only nodes for pinned workloads to avoid that.
[14:25] Emily: For the pilot we need a short test: 48h produce and consume traffic, capture p95 latency, any control-plane metadata traces, and validate no KMS decrypt outside EU.
[14:36] Ava: Agreed. We'll run the pilot and produce a compliance test report.
[14:40] Samir: We'll also want to review the subprocessor contract addendum before approving production.
[14:46] Ava: Noted. We'll share the subprocessor roster and draft addendum.
[15:00] Jordan: Any questions about model quantization or perf that impacts caching?
[15:06] Priya: Not now, more of an ops thing for later.
[15:10] Daniel: One more legal question — indemnity caps tied to data breaches, how do you approach that?
[15:16] Ava: Standard negotiation — we have enterprise tiers for increased liability. We'll surface baseline language in the contract and discuss during legal exchange.
[15:26] Priya: For the pilot we will provide a small subset of production traffic with synthetic patient identifiers; is that acceptable?
[15:34] Jordan: Yes, synthetic or redacted traffic is preferred for pilot.
[15:38] Marta: We'll instrument the pilot to not persist raw prompts to our control plane logs and will provide sample logs for review.
[15:48] Daniel: Great. Any other blockers?
[15:52] Samir: Nothing else on legal for the moment.
[15:55] Ava: OK quick recap — Redwood to share: SOC2 summary, ISO snapshot, KMS integration guide, subprocessor roster, pilot configuration doc. Riverbend to share: network diagram, sample workload, DPA redlines. We'll set a pilot kickoff for week of 6/22.
[16:16] Priya: Confirmed.
[16:18] Emily: Confirmed.
[16:20] Samir: Confirmed.
[16:22] Ava: Action items and next steps noted in chat. I'll follow up with calendar invite and doc links.
[16:30] Jordan: One last operational caveat — if you require EEA-residency for logs and KMS, standard hosted plans may not suffice; we should include sizing and cost delta in the follow-up.
[16:45] Priya: Understood.
[16:50] Ava: Thanks everyone, we'll get the artifacts out today.
[53:50] Ava: Closing notes — legal exchange and pilot start. Thanks all.
---
